summary: הוֹד is majesty: the splendour that marks one as great and is seen and answered with awe and obedience. Above all it is Yahweh’s, who is clothed with הוֹד וְהָדָר and whose הוֹד covers the heavens (Psa 104:1; Hab 3:3); he gives it to the king he sets up, as he gave Solomon “הוֹד of kingship” and as Moses put of his הוֹד on Joshua so that Israel would obey him (1Ch 29:25; Num 27:20), and Zechariah’s Branch “shall bear הוֹד” on his throne as king and priest (Zec 6:13). In a man or a beast it is vigour and fine bearing, which fails before the vision of God (Dan 10:8). The root has no verb in scripture, and no cognate in the other Semitic languages is certain.

words.summary: Twenty-four uses, nearly all in poetry and prophecy: of God, of the king he raises up, and of the vigour of a man, a horse or a tree. It is paired with הָדָר “splendour” eight times. Its meaning rests on its use; the Arabic words recorded beside it are possible links only.

senses.definition: The greatness of Yahweh as it is seen: what he is clothed with, what stands before him and over the heavens, what his works and his voice show, so that it is to be praised and feared.

evidence.note: “Yahweh my God, you are very great; הוֹד וְהָדָר you have put on”: majesty as the garment of his greatness.
הוֹד־וְהָדָר לְפָנָיו, עֹז וְתִפְאֶרֶת בְּמִקְדָּשׁוֹ: before him, set beside strength and beauty in his sanctuary.
The same line in David’s psalm at the bringing up of the ark, with “strength and joy in his place”.
“His name alone is exalted; הוֹדוֹ is over earth and heavens”: majesty is his alone and above all.
“How majestic (אַדִּיר) is your name in all the earth, who have set הוֹדְךָ above the heavens.”
God comes from Teman: “his הוֹד covered the heavens, and his praise (תְּהִלָּתוֹ) filled the earth”.
“Out of the north comes golden splendour; upon God is fearful הוֹד (נוֹרָא הוֹד)”: majesty that makes men fear (37:24).
“Yahweh will cause the הוֹד of his voice to be heard”, with flame of fire, storm and hailstones: his majesty heard in thunder.
“הוֹד־וְהָדָר is his work, and his righteousness stands for ever.”
“The splendour of the glory of your הוֹד (הֲדַר כְּבוֹד הוֹדֶךָ), and your wondrous works, I will meditate on.”
“To you, Yahweh, is the greatness and the might and the beauty and the victory and the הוֹד, for all in heaven and earth is yours; yours is the kingdom.”

senses.definition: The majesty a ruler bears, which marks him as the one to be obeyed. It is not his own: God gives it or withholds it, and one leader can confer some of his on another.

evidence.note: “Yahweh made Solomon very great in the sight of all Israel, and put on him הוֹד מַלְכוּת such as had not been on any king before him.”
A despised one (נִבְזֶה) stands up, “and they have not given him הוֹד מַלְכוּת”, but he seizes the kingdom by flatteries: majesty is given, not taken.
Yahweh to Moses: “you shall put some of your הוֹד on him (Joshua), so that all the congregation of the sons of Israel will obey (יִשְׁמְעוּ)”: the leader’s majesty is what makes the people heed him.
Of the king: “His glory is great through your salvation; הוֹד וְהָדָר you lay upon him”, after “he asked life of you, and you gave it him, length of days for ever and ever” (21:5).
To the king: “Gird your sword on your thigh, mighty one, your הוֹד and your splendour.”
The man whose name is the Branch “shall build the temple of Yahweh, and he shall bear הוֹד, and shall sit and rule on his throne, and shall be a priest on his throne”.
Of Jehoiakim: they will not lament him, “Alas, lord! Alas, his majesty (הֹדֹה)!”: the king dies without the honour due to his office.
Yahweh to Job: “Adorn yourself with pride and height, and put on הוֹד וְהָדָר”: the garment of Psa 104:1, which no man can put on himself.

senses.definition: The vigour and fine bearing of a living thing in its strength: a man’s, a war-horse’s, a flourishing tree’s; the outward show of strength.

evidence.note: Seeing the great vision, “no strength (כֹּחַ) remained in me, and my הוֹד was turned in me to corruption (לְמַשְׁחִית), and I retained no strength”.
The strange woman’s house: “lest you give your הוֹד to others, and your years to the cruel”: the strength of a man’s life spent on her.
Israel restored: “his shoots shall go out, and his הוֹד shall be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Lebanon”.
The war-horse: “the הוֹד of his snorting is terror”, beside “have you given the horse his might (גְּבוּרָה)?” (39:19).
Yahweh of hosts visits his flock, the house of Judah, “and makes them like his horse of הוֹד in battle”.
Jesus “received from God the Father honour and δόξα” at the voice from the majestic glory: majesty given by God to his king (Psa 21:6; 1Ch 29:25).
“Worthy is the Lamb … to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honour and δόξα and blessing”: the ascription of 1Ch 29:11 made to the Lamb.
God “called us by his own δόξα and ἀρετή”.
A royal priesthood, to proclaim “the ἀρεταί of him who called you out of darkness”.

parallels.note: “Splendour, honour”: the pair הוֹד וְהָדָר, of God, of the king, and of what Job cannot put on.
“Glory”: the king’s glory is great, and הוֹד is laid on him; the glory of God’s הוֹד.
“Praise”: his הוֹד covers the heavens and his praise fills the earth.
“Strength”: Daniel’s strength and his הוֹד fail together.

opposites.note: “Despised”: the one to whom הוֹד מַלְכוּת is not given.
“Corruption, ruin”: what Daniel’s הוֹד was turned into.

cognates.gloss: gentleness, favour; a sacred bond, a quality entitling one to respect or reverence
cognates.note: Lane gives هَوَادَةٌ chiefly as gentleness, lenity, favour and reconciliation, but also as “a quality … to be regarded as sacred or inviolable, or rendering one entitled to respect or reverence”, and form V تَهَوَّدَ as allying oneself by such a bond. The last sense comes near the majesty that commands a people’s heed (Num 27:20); the root’s main senses (هَادَ “return, repent”; تَهْوِيد “a gentle, quavering voice”) do not, so the link is recorded as possible only. Arabic h matches Hebrew ה regularly.

cognates.gloss: (of a load) weigh heavily on, burden
cognates.note: آدَهُ “it (a load) oppressed him by its weight, pressed heavily upon him”, with آئِدٌ “burdening” and مَؤُودٌ “burdened”. If related, הוֹד would be weight in the sense of כָּבוֹד “glory”, whose root is “be heavy”, and הוֹד stands beside כָּבוֹד in Psa 21:6 and 145:5. But Arabic ʾ does not regularly answer to Hebrew ה, and the root’s other Arabic sense is “be bent, crooked”, so this is a possible link only.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh has put on הוֹד וְהָדָר as a garment (Psa 104:1); it is before him (Psa 96:6; 1Ch 16:27), it is over earth and heavens because his name alone is exalted (Psa 148:13), and when he comes from Teman it covers the heavens (Hab 3:3). David, offering for the house, says the הוֹד is Yahweh’s, for all in heaven and earth is his (1Ch 29:11). When Job is told to put on הוֹד וְהָדָר himself and humble the proud, he cannot (Job 40:10–14; 42:2–6). In a man הוֹד is vigour, and Daniel’s was turned to corruption before the vision (Dan 10:8). From the verses: majesty belongs to Yahweh by right; a man has none of his own that survives his presence, and holds what he has only as it is given him.

Yahweh gives הוֹד to the king of his choosing: he laid it on Solomon (1Ch 29:25), on the king to whom he gave life, length of days for ever and ever (Psa 21:5–6), and Moses put of his on Joshua so that Israel would obey him (Num 27:20); it is not given to the despised one who takes the kingdom by flatteries (Dan 11:21). Zechariah is told of “the man whose name is the Branch” that he shall build the temple of Yahweh, “and he shall bear הוֹד, and shall sit and rule on his throne, and shall be a priest on his throne” (Zec 6:12–13); the Branch is the righteous one Yahweh raises up for David, who will reign as king (Jer 23:5; 33:15; Zec 3:8). Hebrews says that Jesus is a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek, king and priest in one (Heb 7:1–3, 17; Psa 110:4), and that we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens (Heb 8:1); Peter says that he received honour and glory from God the Father and was seen in his majesty (2Pe 1:16–17). From the verses: the majesty Zechariah’s Branch bears is given him by Yahweh, as it was to the kings before him; the New Testament finds that Branch in Jesus, who holds kingship and priesthood together on one throne.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13. The database keys the root הוד, as the task gave it. One word: הוֹד (e.ay.ab, 24 tokens, including Jer 22:18, spelled הֹדֹה). e.ao.ac (הֹדֹה, “see הוד”) and e.ay.aa (the root) are cross-references with no tokens, not claimed. Names formed with הוד are left for names/: עַמִּיהוּד Ammihud (p.dj.aj; drafted with this entry; p.dj.al עמיחור is its Kethiv at 2Sa 13:37), אֲבִיהוּד Abihud (a.ae.ak), אֲחִיהוּד Ahihud (a.ck.ai), אִישׁ הוֹד Ishhod (a.da.ad), הוֹד Hod (e.ay.ac, 1Ch 7:37), הוֹדִיָּה Hodiah (e.ay.ae), הודוה / הוֹדְיָה Hodevah (e.ay.ad, e.ay.af) and הוֹדַוְיָה(וּ) Hodaviah. Open question: Hodiah, Hodevah and Hodaviah may rather be formed from ידה “give thanks, confess” (hiphil הוֹדָה), not from הוֹד; check before writing their name entries. No verb הוד occurs in scripture; Wiktionary’s modern Hebrew הֵד “echo” and תְּהוּדָה “resonance” are later Hebrew and not used. Cognates: no certain cognate found. Lane’s هود (return, repent; gentleness; a gentle voice) and اود (weigh upon; be bent) are recorded as possible only; هيد (move, frighten; cries to camels) does not share the meaning and is not recorded. No Akkadian, Ugaritic, Phoenician, Aramaic or Syriac word was found (the Peshitta has no cognate root; Oracc candidates under d/wd/yd mean “know”, “single”, “arm”, none “majesty”). Leads not followed: Ugaritic (Segert, Fisher) and South Arabian not checked. Greek: the Septuagint also renders הוֹד by ἐξομολόγησις (Psa 96:6; 104:1; 111:3), which the New Testament never uses, and once each by ἰσχύς, ζωή, εὐπρεπής and ἰδού; not recorded. No New Testament verse quotes a verse with הוֹד; the δόξα and ἀρετή verses are thematic, not quotations. The doctrine ‘the-branch-bears-majesty’ applies Zec 6:13 to Jesus through Hebrews and 2 Peter; Hebrews does not cite Zec 6 itself.
